children: Aluminium prices rose on Thursday, buoyed by continued supply tightness and a slight improvement in economic risk sentiment, which also boosted other industrial metals.
on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.32% at $3,294 a metric ton by 0700 GMT. Earlier, it touched $3,306.50, its highest since August 13.
The most-traded aluminium contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange

"Aluminium is being supported by a combination of physical destocking, expectations of a seasonal improvement in Chinese demand and relatively constrained supply growth," said Rupankar RM, head of market research and data intelligence at AL Circle.

Despite hopes for returning supply from the big producers in the Middle East, analysts expect the market to remain in deficit this year, and LME stocks (MALSTX-TOTAL) of the light metal, widely used in manufacturing, consumer goods and automobiles, remain close to a 36-year low.
Elsewhere, copper and zinc, which led Wednesday's industrial metals losses on cooling supply concerns and a macroeconomic risk-off, had uneven gains.

The key LME cash-to-three-month copper spread (CMCU0-3) remained in backwardation on Wednesday, signaling tight availability but tightened to $87.56 a ton, its narrowest since August 21.
